master.title: UPDATE: RUSSIA-UKRAINE CONFLICT, March 31, as at 09:00 (Msk)
master.content:
Russian, German experts to hold additional talks on gas payments, Kremlin says following Putin-Scholz call

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin and German Chancellor Olaf Scholz have spoken over the phone, the Kremlin press service said.

"Vladimir Putin substantively informed the chancellor of the decision to transition to payments for gas delivered to Germany, among other places, in Russian rubles. This change in the arrangement for making payments is being introduced due to the currency reserves of the Bank of Russia being frozen by members of the European Union in violation of the norms of international law. It was noted that this decision should not lead to a worsening of contract conditions for European importers of Russian gas, and it was agreed that experts of the two countries will hold additional talks on this subject," the press service said.

"Vladimir Putin and Olaf Scholz exchanged opinions on the latest round of talks between Russian and Ukrainian representatives held the day before in Istanbul. Ensuring the safe evacuation of civilians from areas where hostilities are taking place, primarily Mariupol, was also given consideration," it said.

Putin gives explanations to Italian PM on settlements for gas supplies

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin has spoken with Italian Prime Minister Mario Draghi by telephone, the Kremlin press service said.

"At Mario Draghi's request, Vladimir Putin briefed him on the progress of the talks between Russian and Ukrainian representatives, another round of which was held the previous day in Istanbul," the statement said.

"Explanations were also given regarding the decision to switch to rubles in settlements for natural gas supplies to a number of countries, including Italy," the press service said.

Lavrov hails results of Istanbul talks as a move forward

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - The results of the Russia-Ukraine talks held in Istanbul are a positive move forward, with Kyiv understanding that the matter of Crimea and Donbas is closed, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Wednesday.

"We are seeing the results of yesterday's talks in Istanbul as a positive move forward. This is not a final result yet," Lavrov told reporters.

"I consider it major progress that Ukrainian negotiators have confirmed the need to guarantee Ukraine's non-nuclear, non-aligned status and their security without NATO, and equally that our Ukrainian counterparts understand that the Crimea and Donbas issues are finally solved," he said.

Lavrov on U.S. skepticism related to Russia decreasing its military activity in Ukraine: U.S. itself has its own issues with deeds versus words

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has declined to comment on the statements of U.S. officials who earlier expressed skepticism with regard to Russian plans to scale back military activity in Ukraine and noted that the U.S.'s deeds do not reflect its words as a rule.

The Russian foreign minister was asked on Wednesday what he thinks of the statements of U.S. officials who said, commenting on Russian plans to reduce military activity in Ukraine, that there is a difference between things being said and being done, and suggested that a threat remains, and that U.S. President Joe Biden said that one has to wait and see if Russia's actions will be finalized before assessing them. "I can't think or fantasize for U.S. President Joe Biden, and I can't fantasize for Secretary of State Antony Blinken. If you talk about who has differences between deeds and words, then I just won't mention the great number of cases right now, where the U.S. said one thing and did something quite different," Lavrov told reporters during his visit to the Tunxi district of China's Anhui province.

Core objectives on Kyiv, Chernihiv fronts achieved - Russian Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russia has achieved its main objectives on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts, the Defense Ministry's spokesperson Igor Konashenkov said.

"All main tasks of the Russian Armed Forces on the Kyiv and Chernihiv directions are completed," Konashenkov told a briefing on Wednesday.

"The aim of troop re-grouping is to step up action on priority directions, chiefly the conclusion of the operation of the full liberation of Donbas," he said.

Russian army regrouping after achieving objectives near Kyiv, Chernihiv - defense ministry

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russian troops have fulfilled their missions on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts and proceeded to regrouping, the Defense Ministry's spokesman Igor Konashenkov said.

"Planned troop regrouping is taking place on the Kyiv and Chernihiv directions. At the initial stage of the special military operation conducted by the Russian Armed Forces in Donbas and Ukraine, the plan was to force the enemy to concentrate its forces, means, resources and military hardware to hold big settlements on these directions, including Kyiv," Konashenkov told a briefing on Wednesday.

"To shackle them on the battlefield and, without storming those cities, to avoid civilian casualties, to strike at armed formations of the Kyiv regime to prevent it from using these forces on the main direction of our military action: Donbas. All these goals have been attained," he added.

Russian Defense Ministry reports about 70 Ukrainian military targets destroyed over past day

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Operational-tactical and unmanned aircraft hit 69 Ukrainian military targets over the past day, Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov said.

"Three command posts, two multiple rocket launchers, eight ammunition and missile-artillery weapon depots, and 52 strongholds and areas of concentrated military equipment are among them," Konashenkov said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

"In total, 124 aircraft and 77 helicopters, 214 anti-aircraft missile systems, 323 unmanned aerial vehicles, 1,767 tanks and other combat armored vehicles, 186 multiple rocket launchers, 741 field artillery guns and mortars, and 1,657 special military vehicles have been destroyed since the launch of the special military operation," he said.

[Russian] air defense forces destroyed two Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles in the areas of Balakleya and Verhnetoretske in the past 24 hours, the Russian Defense Ministry said.

Baltic Fleet holds combat readiness drill

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - The Baltic Fleet's military command bodies, units and formations have begun a combat readiness drill in the Kaliningrad region.

"The military command bodies, units and formations are practicing achieving the highest degree of combat readiness, emergency preparation of military personnel and equipment, departures for assigned areas, and the execution of combat tasks," the Fleet stated on Wednesday.

"Led by Baltic Fleet Commander Vice Admiral Viktor Liina [the troops] are practicing aspects of preparation and control of units and formations in various tactical operations," the statement said.

"More than five command posts have been set up since the drill began to control subordinated troops and interact with Army Corps and Western Military District staffs."

The command post exercise involves over 1,500 troops and up to 80 units of weapons, military and special equipment, the Fleet said.

Russian Defense Ministry says humanitarian situation most critical in Ukraine's Kharkiv

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) -The most critical situation is in the city of Kharkiv, Russian National Defense Control Center head Mikhail Mizintsev said.

"The humanitarian situation in a number of populated localities controlled by Kyiv is continuing to deteriorate rapidly, and the most critical situation is in Kharkiv today," Mizintsev said on Wednesday.

A curfew has been imposed in the city, he said.

"Fearing provocations on the part of nationalists, local residents have to hide in basements. Many houses have been left without heating, electricity and gas. Utility companies do no restoration work. Hospitals deny civilians medical treatment, only providing medical care to members of the Ukrainian Armed Forces and territorial defense combatants. There are no vitally important medicines available in pharmacies. Food stores operate two or three hours a day, and there are almost no shoppers in there, as many people have just run out of money," Mizintsev said.

The Ukrainian Security Service (SBU) is making mass arrests, he said.

"People try not to talk on the phone or via social media. They are cautious in what they say, because the SBU are making mass arrests among civilians," he said.

In order to save Kharkiv residents, "urgent decisions aimed at stabilizing the humanitarian situation are needed," he said.

The Russian side is asking international organizations to make the Ukrainian authorities meet their humanitarian commitments in Kharkiv and other populated localities of the country, he said.

"We appeal to the chiefs of the United Nations, OSCE, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other international organizations and strongly request to use the authority and potential of your organizations to force the Kyiv authorities to meet their humanitarian obligations, and not only in Kharkiv but also in other populated localities of Ukraine," Mizintsev said.

Kyiv declares 4 additional humanitarian corridors from Zaporizhzhya on Wed - Russian Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - The Ukrainian side on Wednesday declared four additional humanitarian corridors from Zaporizhzhya, and Russia agreed on them, head of Russia's National Defense Control Center Mikhail Mizintsev said.

"The Ukrainian authorities have declared four additional routes from Zaporizhzhya for the current 24 hours," Mizintsev said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

"Russia agreed to the Ukrainian side's proposals without any additional conditions," he said.

"The Russian Armed Forces and the formations of the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics are strictly observing the temporary ceasefire on all routes, including those declared by the Ukrainian side," Mizintsev said.

He also said that the Kyiv authorities continue to obstruct the evacuation of civilians and foreign nationals to the territory of Russia.

"The Russian Federation is continuing its purposeful and coordinated operation to evacuate the local population and foreign citizens to safe areas, as well as carrying out a set of measures to provide humanitarian aid to the population in the territories of Ukraine liberated from neo-Nazis," Mizintsev said.

The Russian military has opened humanitarian corridors from Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv, and Mariupol at 10 a.m. every day since March 4, he said. "One humanitarian corridor [from each of these cities] to the Russian Federation, and one more [from each of these cities] via Kyiv-controlled territories toward Ukraine's western borders," Mizintsev said.

Russian military ready to declare temporary ceasefire in Mariupol Thursday

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russia is ready to declare temporary ceasefire in Mariupol and open a humanitarian corridor toward Zaporizhzhya, providing Kyiv has met several conditions, the Russian military said.

"Russia's Armed Forces are declaring temporary ceasefire from 10 a.m. March 31, 2022, purely for humane purposes, and opening an additional humanitarian corridor for the evacuation of civilians and foreign nationals from Mariupol to Zaporizhzhya (with a stop in Berdiansk)," the head of the National Defense Control Center, Mikhail Mizintsev, told a briefing on Wednesday.

Russia will not open the corridor unless Ukraine has formally agreed in writing to comply with several conditions and confirmed the actual ceasefire.

"We demand from Kyiv authorities strict compliance with the following conditions for the creation of a humanitarian corridor: guaranteed unconditional compliance with the temporary ceasefire within established times, of which it is to notify the Russian side and representatives from the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) by 6 a.m. March 31, 2022," Mizintsev said.

Also, Kyiv must provide safe passage for evacuation buses on the agreed-upon route, especially between Mariupol and Berdiansk, he said.

"At the same time we report that at present that the Berdiansk-Mariupol section of the route is being systemically attacked by Ukraine's armed forces and nationalist battalions with mortar launchers and large-caliber machine guns," Mizintsev said.

It is proposed to conduct the humanitarian operation with direct UNHCR and ICRC participation, he said.

Russian Defense Ministry says it has list of people employed by Pentagon who worked in biological laboratories in Ukraine (

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - The Russian Defense Ministry has said it has a list of people working for Pentagon and contractor companies, who took part in developing components for biological weapons in Ukraine.

"Upon studying new materials, experts of the radiological, chemical and biological defense forces have identified the officials who took part in creating components for biological weapons. They are division heads and employees of the U.S. Department of Defense and its main contractor companies," Russian Defense Ministry spokesperson Igor Konashenkov said on Wednesday.

"The Russian defense Ministry is continuing to study documents received from the employees of Ukrainian biological laboratories about the secret military-biological activities of the U.S. in Ukraine," he said.

"Some journalists' investigations in the Western press show that these companies were directly linked to the son of the current U.S. president, Hunter Biden," Konashenkov said.

"As a result of the ongoing special military operation, studies stopped in several Ukrainian bio laboratories which were working on the orders of the Pentagon with strains of dangerous contagious-disease pathogens," he said.

"A number of documents obtained from these laboratories indicates that the identities of test persons have been concealed and there is a serious risk for their lives," he said.

"Documents indicative of the Kyiv authorities' plans to use unmanned aerial vehicles capable of carrying and dispersing deadly chemical substances are especially interesting. Exposed facts prove that the Kyiv regime seriously considered the possibility of using biological weapons against the population of Donbas and the Russian Federation," Konashenkov said.

Pentagon representative John Kirby said earlier that the U.S. was not developing biological weapons in Ukraine.

LPR troops continue advance on Severodonetsk - Russian Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - The forces of the Luhansk People's Republic (LPR) are continuing the advance on Severodonetsk, Russian Defense Ministry spokesperson Igor Konashenkov said

"Units of the [LPR] are continuing the advance on Severodonetsk. Fighting is underway to clear the village of Zhitlovka," Konashenkov told a briefing on Wednesday.

The Ukrainian military are "incurring serious losses on the Severonetsk direction," he said.

"The disruption of transport communications has blocked their refill capacity. During the day more than 50 nationalists, two tanks, three IFVs and two field rocket artillery depots were destroyed in the area," Konashenkov said.

Russian Deputy FM Vershinin, ICRC president discuss DPR, LPR, Ukraine, humanitarian cooperation

MOSCOW. March 30 (Interfax) - Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Vershinin and International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) President Peter Maurer have discussed humanitarian cooperation in a phone call, the Russian Foreign Ministry website said.

"Following the meeting between [Russian Foreign Minister] Sergei Lavrov and Peter Maurer in Moscow on March 24, Sergei Vershinin and the ICRC president compared notes on the situation in the DPR, the LPR [the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics], and in Ukraine, confirming the focus on continuing cooperation between Russia and the Committee in resolving humanitarian issues, in particular, protecting civilians, organizing and operating humanitarian corridors, and assisting refugees," the statement said.

Belarus, Russia discuss countering unfriendly actions of other countries, coordination of operations of diplomatic missions

MINSK. March 30 (Interfax) - Belarusian Deputy Foreign Minister Yury Ambrazevich discussed with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Vershinin and head of the Russian Federal Agency for the Commonwealth of Independent States Affairs, Compatriots Residing Abroad, and International Humanitarian Cooperation (Rossotrudnichestvo) Yevgeny Primakov efforts to counter unfriendly initiatives against the two countries in Moscow on Wednesday.

"During the meeting, the Russian Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the strategic unity of the positions of Belarus and Russia on the place and role of the United Nations in the modern context. They discussed joint counteraction to unfriendly initiatives against Belarus and Russia as part of international organizations," the press service for the Belarusian Foreign Ministry said.

"An agreement was reached to improve the mechanisms of urgent coordination between the foreign missions of the two countries on this issue. The parties also discussed the prospects of implementing a number of UN-funded international technical assistance projects for Belarus's sustainable development," the ministry said.

Besides, during the meeting in Rossotrudnichestvo, the parties discussed the possibilities of stepping up the efforts of the two countries to promote among compatriots residing abroad "common approaches toward historical events, topical issues of the present day and in general toward the values that traditionally unite Belarusian and Russian peoples," the ministry said.

"Ways to intensify cultural and educational exchange, as well as the assistance to refugees from Ukraine with the involvement of Rossotrudnichestvo's potential were discussed," the Belarusian Foreign Ministry said.

Zelensky, Biden discuss defense assistance for Ukraine

KYIV. March 30 (Interfax) - Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and his American counterpart Joe Biden have discussed Washington's macro-financial, humanitarian and defense assistance for Ukraine and further anti-Russian sanctions.

"Just finished an hour-long conversation with President of the U.S. {We] shared an assessment of the situation on the battlefield and at the negotiating table. Talked about specific defensive support, a new package of enhanced sanctions, macro-financial and humanitarian aid," Zelensky tweeted on Wednesday evening.

candidate.content:
Ukraine created mine threat to civilian vessels of Black Sea countries - Russian Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. March 31 (Interfax) - The Russian Defense Ministry has denied Kyiv's statement that Russian troops have installed mines in the Black Sea.

The old mines in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov were installed by Ukrainian troops, some of those mines came off their anchors and their location is unknown, Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov said on Thursday.

"The remnants of the minesweeping forces of the Ukrainian Navy installed some 420 old YaM-1 sea anchor mines in the Black Sea and in the Sea of Azov, 370 in the Black Sea and 50 in the Sea of Azov, in the period between February 25 and March 4," Konashenkov said.

"As a result of storms in the Black Sea and due to the poor technical condition, the cables with seabed anchors holding some ten Ukrainian mines were torn. Since then, the Ukrainian mines have freely drifted in the western part of the Black Sea southward under the influence of wind and surface currents," he said.

One Ukrainian mine has recently been neutralized by Turkish sailors and the other was neutralized in the Romanian territorial waters, he said.

"No one can know where the remaining Ukrainian mines are now drifting," Konashenkov said.

The Ukrainian authorities have created "a direct mine threat to transport and cargo vessels of all Black Sea countries," he said.

The Ukrainian authorities are blocking 68 civilian vessels in ports, Konashenkov said.

DPR administration created in Mariupol

DONETSK. March 31 (Interfax) - A Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) administration has been created in Mariupol, for which fierce fighting is going on.

"I decree to create a local administration of the Donetsk People's Republic, the administration of the city of Mariupol," DPR leader Denis Pushilin said in his decree.

Russia launched "a special military operation" in Ukraine on February 24.

Russian president briefs Norwegian PM on military operation in Ukraine, Russia-Ukraine talks - Kremlin

MOSCOW. March 31 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin has spoken with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store over the phone, the Kremlin's press service said.

"Putin has given a detailed account of the reasons for the special military operation, which aims at protecting Donbas, as well as its goals and objectives. Emphasis has been put on humanitarian affairs, first and foremost the effort towards providing security of the civilian population and opening humanitarian corridors for the evacuation of civilians from combat zones, including Mariupol," the press service said.

The Russian president "has also informed [the Norwegian prime minister] about talks between the Russian and Ukrainian representatives, the latest round of which has recently taken place in Istanbul," it said.

The interlocutors agreed to stay in touch, the press service said.

Kremlin concerned about Washington's lack of understanding of Russian decision-making mechanism - Peskov

MOSCOW. March 31 (Interfax) - U.S. officials have no idea of what is really going on in the Kremlin and how decisions are made there, which may have bad consequences and lead to erroneous decisions of the United States, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

"This is a source of our concern. It looks like neither the Department of State nor the Pentagon know what is really happening in the Kremlin. They simply do not understand what is going on in the Kremlin. They do not understand President [Vladimir] Putin. They do not understand the decision-making mechanism. They do not understand our workstyle," Peskov said at a press conference on Thursday.

He thus commented on recent statements by U.S. representatives who said that Putin was not receiving complete information about the special operation in Ukraine and felt misled.

"We do not just regret this. This is a source of our concern. Because such an utter lack of understanding is the reason why erroneous, rash decisions are made with very bad consequences," he said.

Media outlets said earlier, citing Pentagon spokesman John Kirby, that Putin was not fully aware of the real progress of the special operation in Ukraine.

Russian parliamentary commission to mull possible connection between bio-labs in Ukraine, epidemics in Russia on Apr 4

MOSCOW. March 31 (Interfax) - The next meeting of the Russian parliamentary commission investigating operations of biological laboratories in Ukraine will mule a possible connection between the labs and biological and bacteriological threats that emerged in Russia in recent years, Federation Council Deputy Speaker Konstantin Kosachyov said.

"Our next meeting will be held on Monday to analyze what is happening or has been happening in the Russian territory over the recent years from the angle of biological and bacteriological threats - epidemics and pandemics - and to establish the causes and consequences. Because, some of those or, maybe, all of them, could be directly related to the operation of U.S. biological laboratories in the Ukrainian territory," Kosachyov told reporters on Thursday after the first meeting of the commission.

There was a follow-up question whether Kosachyov thought that the coronavirus pandemic could be related to the operation of biological laboratories in Ukraine.

"No, we absolutely do not raise the question this way. All I have said is various sorts of epidemics and pandemics. Let us not forestall the nature of our work. We are open to the information provided by our interlocutors and partners and we will draw our conclusions exclusively on the basis of that information," he said.

"We do not doctor our conclusions so that they fit the task. We understand that our final report will be relevant only if it is depoliticized, so to say, and if it fully relies on facts established in the course of our parliamentary inquiry and on evidence," Kosachyov said.

By law, a parliamentary inquiry can last for up to one year, but the commission will try to work faster, he said.

"As to organizing our work, the parliamentary inquiry law of 2015 allows us to do the work during a calendar year, but we have agreed to work as fast as we can: we seek at least not to exceed these deadlines and at best to present our conclusions as fast as we can," Kosachyov said.

Kosachyov co-chairs the commission conducting this parliamentary inquiry.

llm_judgement.note: Different dispatches in the same running series; they cover different events and contain distinct article text.
